source.title: Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization
source.authors: Sanjeev Arora; N. Cohen; Wei Hu; Yuping Luo

record.tranche_reason: Tests implicit regularization and held-out reconstruction in deep linear matrix factorization, a new setting relative to the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper’s introduction mentions random-label fitting and generalization as prior work, but reports no random-label experiment of its own. Its own matrix-completion and matrix-sensing results measure reconstruction and implicit low-rank bias; these do not test any listed version directly.
record.test_reason: The study measures reconstruction and implicit low-rank bias in deep linear matrix factorization. None of V1–V8 concerns this depth-dependent reconstruction effect. Random-label fitting, batch-size effects and generalization measures appear only as background; the study conducts no corresponding tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Theory and experiments indicate that depth strengthens an implicit tendency toward low-rank solutions and can improve matrix recovery. The authors question simple norm-based explanations and propose studying optimization trajectories; they do not prove that every norm-based characterization is impossible.
record.recipe_differences: Deep linear matrix factorization trained by full-batch gradient descent for matrix completion and sensing; not the listed image or language classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth changes the strength of the low-rank bias. In the nuclear-norm experiments, initialization size affected depth 2, while smaller initialization had no observable effect on depths 3 and 4. The number of observed entries changed whether factorization solutions approached the minimum nuclear-norm solution.

fits_no_version.finding: Depths 3 and 4 outperform depth 2 on synthetic matrix completion with few observations; deeper factorizations favor lower effective rank despite higher nuclear norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested deep linear matrix-completion settings, increasing depth strengthens low-rank bias and can improve reconstruction when observations are scarce.

fits_no_version.finding: With sufficiently many observations, all tested factorization depths approach the minimum nuclear-norm solution and ground truth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested data-rich matrix-completion settings, different factorization depths achieve accurate recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic matrix completion and subsampled MovieLens experiments show stronger separation between large and small singular values with greater depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth in the tested matrix factorizations changes optimization dynamics toward solutions of lower effective rank.

record.problems: The reported experiments use matrix completion and sensing, including synthetic random low-rank matrices and a subsampled MovieLens matrix. Figure values are primarily qualitative in the supplied text; error bars are described as indiscernible and the completion and sensing comparisons use three random-seed trials. The theoretical nuclear-norm result requires commuting measurement matrices and specified existence and optimality assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: Matrix-sensing figures and related depth-wise results are not separately extracted because they supplement the matrix-completion findings with the same qualitative pattern; the text supplies no numerical values. Figure 3 also plots singular-vector alignment for depth 2, but this is not a listed version and is not needed for the proposed findings.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit the training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay and optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T3 requires a result on a listed version; a new setting involving generalization alone is insufficient. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, although their qualitative findings are supported. Appendix D defines reconstruction error over the entire matrix, rather than exclusively held-out entries. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels for the listed image classifiers.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test error as width changes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers on image or language benchmarks.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: depth-2 matrix factorization
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on observed entries with no explicit regularization; reconstruction error evaluated during matrix completion.

conditions.key: learning rate and initialization standard deviation

rows.measure: normalized Frobenius reconstruction error on the matrix completion task; the text describes the result as reconstruction error without stating a separate numerical test-error value
rows.baseline: depth-3 and depth-4 factorizations are the stated comparators
rows.value: with few observed entries, depth-2 is significantly outperformed by depths 3 and 4
rows.uncertainty: standard deviations over multiple trials; error bars described as indiscernible
rows.note: The paper’s description supports the qualitative comparison; precise plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative depth comparison is supported, but it measures no listed version; worse reconstruction than deeper models does not justify a partial claim state.
